newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBM S.Africa shares tumble on poor results.
newsitem.headline: IBM S.Africa shares tumble on poor results.

text.p: Shares in IBM South Africa Group Ltd fell sharply on Monday after the company reported poor results for the year ending December 31.
The stock was last trading down 315 cents at 1,425 after touching a morning low of 1,350.
IBM reported earnings per share of 55.8 cents from the 69.4 cents it attained in 1995, while its dividend was flat at 26 cents.
Dealers said IBM had misjudged its entry into the highly competitive lower-end computing market with its launch of the PC-100 machine last year.

"The results are lower than expected. IBM finds itself in the wrong sector of the IT (Information Technology) industry. It's focused more on the hardware side where there is no growth at the moment," one dealer commented.
"The software sector is where things are picking up," he added.

Another dealer said the worrying thing for the market was how much stock IBM still had left of the failed new low-tier personal computer. IBM said the unsuccessful launch of the product was largely responsible for a fall in attributable income to 73.8 million rand from 101.0 million rand.
"They (IBM) misjudged the competition from people like Apple and others who have focused for a long time at the lower-end market. IBM got out of their normal upper-end market," he said.
"I expect their interim results to pick up," he added, predicting the share could recover to around 1,450 by the close on Monday.
